title: Christ reveals us (Gaudium et Spes 22)
hookLine: Christ fully reveals humanity to itself
tomorrow: is the self something you find, or something you give?

lines: QUIZZES, SIGNS, A FEED THAT GUESSES.
cards: Personality quizzes. Star signs. A feed that guesses what you'll want before you do.
There's no shortage of offers to tell you who you are. Gaudium et Spes has an answer of its own, and it doesn't start with you. It starts with a person.
Jewish teachers, in the Mishnah, asked the same question, and answered it with a coin.

teach.b: The question is old: what is a human being? Paragraph twenty-two answers by looking somewhere unexpected.

Christ, it says, by revealing the Father and the Father's love, fully reveals humanity to itself and makes its highest calling clear. Notice the direction: not from us up to God, but from Christ back to us.

Then it gets physical. By becoming human, the Son of God has in some way united himself with every person. He worked with human hands, thought with a human mind, acted by human choice, loved with a human heart.
And it reaches past the Church's walls: this holds, the text says, for all people of good will, in whose hearts grace works unseen. Here's a neighbor asking the same question.
The Mishnah, a collection of Jewish teaching, wonders why God began humanity with one single person. One answer: so that no one could ever say to another, my ancestor was greater than yours.

teach.h: ONE SEAL, NO TWO COINS ALIKE.
teach.b: Another: a ruler stamps many coins with one seal and they all come out alike, but God stamped every human with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another.
So each person may say, the world was created for my sake. What's shared: every face carries a likeness no one else has, and at the root, no one ranks above anyone.
What's honestly different: Catholics read the full meaning of a human being in Christ, God made human.
Jewish tradition doesn't hold that God became a man; it reads that worth in the one Creator and the first person he made.

how: Catholics often pray with the Gospels, slowly picturing a scene from Jesus' life and letting it shape how they see themselves.

games.q: a friend says, "i'll know who i am once i land the right job." where does Gaudium et Spes 22 point instead?
o: to the right job, once it finally comes along.
to Christ, who shows people who they're meant to be.
to a personality test, taken honestly and often.
games.why: the council says Christ, revealing the Father's love, fully reveals humanity to itself and makes its highest calling clear. a job can't do that.

practice: Rest your hands open on your knees and look at them: the lines, a scar, whatever they did today. The council says Christ worked with hands like these. Then let them rest, palms up, and let your breath be the only work for a while.

wordCard.voice: Christ reveals us. Gaudium et Spes 22: looking at Christ, people learn who they are meant to be.

orig.note: Latin, 'shows' or 'reveals': in the council's text, Christ fully shows humanity to itself.

carryVoice: Your line: revealed to ourselves. Every face carries a stamp no one else has. Go gently.
